+# Contributing
+
+Thanks for helping save tokens. The most useful contribution is a new filter, or
+a better one, together with real fixtures.
+
+## Ground rules
+
+- Everything in the repository is in English: code, comments, docs, commit
+  messages, CLI strings and test names.
+- Never hide information without a trace. A filter may drop lines only because
+  the runner always prints the path to the full log. A filter must keep
+  everything needed to act on a failure: which test, where it failed, and why.
+- When in doubt, return `None`. The runner then falls back to the generic
+  filter.
+- Keep it fast and dependency-light. Do not spawn processes from filters, and do
+  not add async runtimes.
+- No telemetry, ever.
+
+## Adding a filter
+
+1. **Capture real output.** Run the tool once passing and once failing, then
+   save both outputs with stderr merged and colours off:
+
+   ```sh
+   NO_COLOR=1 mytool test > crates/hk/tests/fixtures/mytool/pass.txt 2>&1
+   NO_COLOR=1 mytool test > crates/hk/tests/fixtures/mytool/fail.txt 2>&1
+   ```
+
+   Replace personal paths (`/home/you/...`) with `/work`, and remove tokens and
+   hostnames. Do not hand-edit anything else. Fixtures are stored byte-exact
+   (see `.gitattributes`).
+
+2. **Write the module** `crates/hk/src/filters/mytool.rs`:
+
+   ```rust
+   use super::{Cmd, Filter};
+   use crate::config::Limits;
+
+   pub struct MyTool;
+
+   impl Filter for MyTool {
+       fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "mytool" }
+
+       fn detect(&self, cmd: &Cmd) -> bool {
+           cmd.program == "mytool" && cmd.subcommand() == Some("test")
+       }
+
+       fn filter(&self, output: &str, exit: i32, limits: &Limits) -> Option<String> {
+           // `output` is already ANSI-stripped with CRLF normalised.
+           // Return None if you do not recognise it.
+           todo!()
+       }
+   }
+   ```
+
+   Conventions: on success, print one line (`✓ N passed`). On failure, print a
+   `✗` summary line, then one `FAIL <name>` block per failure, with at most
+   `limits.stack_lines` indented lines. Cap lists at `limits.max_errors` with
+   `text::push_capped` (`+N more`).
+
+3. **Register it.** Add `pub mod mytool;` and `&mytool::MyTool` to `registry()`
+   in `crates/hk/src/filters/mod.rs`. Add a line to the
+   `registry_routes_commands` test.
+
+4. **Add the fixture cases** to `CASES` in `crates/hk/tests/fixtures.rs`. Each
+   case is the fixture directory, the case name, the command line that
+   produced it, and its exit code.
+
+5. **Review the snapshots:**
+
+   ```sh
+   cargo test               # new snapshots are written as .snap.new
+   cargo insta review       # or: INSTA_UPDATE=always cargo test
+   ```
+
+   Read each snapshot. Would you be able to fix the failure from the compact
+   output alone? If not, keep more lines.
+
+6. Update the filter table in `README.md` and add a line to `CHANGELOG.md`
+   under `Unreleased`.
+
+## Before opening a PR
+
+```sh
+cargo fmt --all
+cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
+cargo test --workspace
+```
+
+CI runs these on Linux, macOS and Windows.
+
+## Releasing (maintainers)
+
+1. Bump the version in `Cargo.toml`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `bin/hk`
+   (`VERSION=`), then move `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` under the new version.
+2. Merge, then tag `vX.Y.Z` and push the tag. The release workflow checks that
+   the versions match, builds all six targets, and publishes the assets with
+   their `.sha256` files and `SHA256SUMS`.

 # hook-n-hooks
 
-Token-saving hooks for Claude Code. Work in progress.
+Token-saving hooks for Claude Code. `hook-n-hooks` is a Claude Code plugin
+backed by one small Rust binary, `hk`. It cuts the tokens Claude spends reading
+test runs, build errors and package installs. It formats the files Claude edits,
+and it gives Claude a compact map of the repository at session start. It does
+not block anything: blocking and safety are what Claude Code's own permission
+modes are for.
+
+Nothing is hidden without a trace. Whenever output is compacted, the first line
+Claude sees is the path to the full log on your disk. There is no telemetry, and
+stats stay on your machine.
+
+## What it saves
+
+| Hook | What it does |
+| --- | --- |
+| **PreToolUse (Bash)** | Rewrites a known command to `hk run -- <cmd>`. `hk run` runs it, saves the full log and prints a compact result. The exit code is kept exactly. |
+| **PostToolUse (Edit/Write)** | Formats and autofixes **only the touched file** with rustfmt, gofmt, ruff, biome or prettier/eslint, if installed. It reports only the issues it could not fix. |
+| **SessionStart** | Adds a repo map: a 2-level tree, the detected stack, and the resolved build/test/lint commands. |
+
+The Bash filters:
+
+| Filter | Commands | On success | On failure |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| `cargo_test` | `cargo test` | `✓ 342 passed` | each failing test, its panic location and assertion |
+| `pytest` | `pytest`, `python -m pytest`, `uv run pytest` | `✓ 2 passed` | each failing test, `>`/`E` lines, `file:line` |
+| `js_test` | `vitest run`, `jest`, `npm/pnpm/yarn test` | `✓ 1 passed` | test name, assertion, diff, first stack frame |
+| `go_test` | `go test` | `✓ 3 package(s) ok` | `--- FAIL` names plus `t.Errorf` lines |
+| `deno_bun_test` | `deno test`, `bun test` | `✓ 1 passed` | test name, error, diff, location |
+| `build` | `cargo build/check/clippy`, `tsc`, `go build/vet` | `✓ build ok` | one `file:line: msg` per diagnostic, de-duplicated, max 20 + `+N more` |
+| `install` | `npm/pnpm/yarn/bun install`, `cargo fetch`, `pip`, `uv`, `poetry` | the result lines | errors kept; progress bars and deprecation noise dropped |
+| `generic` | fallback, or commands listed in `rewrite.generic_commands` | output unchanged if short | head 30 + tail 30 lines |
+
+ANSI colours are always stripped. If a filter does not recognise an output, the
+generic filter is used instead. A "summary" that would be longer than the
+original output is never used.
+
+### Before and after
+
+These numbers come from the snapshot tests over real captured outputs
+(`crates/hk/tests/snapshots/`). Tokens are estimated as characters / 4.
+
+`cargo test` with two failing tests: 909 chars (~227 tokens) become 250 chars
+(~62 tokens), plus the log line.
+
+```
+running 4 tests
+test tests::fails_one ... FAILED
+test tests::adds_neg ... ok
+...
+---- tests::fails_one stdout ----
+
+thread 'tests::fails_one' (12345) panicked at src/lib.rs:7:30:
+assertion `left == right` failed: math is broken
+  left: 4
+ right: 5
+note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
+...
+test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
+```
+
+becomes
+
+```
+[hk] log: ~/.local/share/hk/logs/1795487589516338550-1540218-cargo_test.log
+✗ 2 failed, 2 passed
+FAIL tests::fails_one
+  panicked at src/lib.rs:7:30:
+  assertion `left == right` failed: math is broken
+  left: 4
+  right: 5
+FAIL tests::panics
+  panicked at src/lib.rs:8:62:
+  index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 3
+```
+
+More examples from the fixtures:
+
+| Fixture | Raw chars | Compact chars |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| `cargo test`, passing | 663 | 10 |
+| `pytest`, passing | 369 | 10 |
+| `pytest`, 1 failure | 810 | 163 |
+| `cargo build`, 3 errors | 1249 | 168 |
+| `vitest run`, 1 failure | 726 | 183 |
+| `pnpm install` with progress bars | 1519 | 136 |
+
+The log line adds about 80 characters to every wrapped command. Real projects
+produce far longer outputs than these small fixtures, so the savings grow with
+the size of the suite. Run `hk stats` to see your own numbers.
+
+## Install
+
+In Claude Code:
+
+```
+/plugin marketplace add Rixmerz/hook-n-hooks
+/plugin install hook-n-hooks@hook-n-hooks
+```
+
+On Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, this one line does both:
+
+```
+/plugin install hook-n-hooks --marketplace Rixmerz/hook-n-hooks
+```
+
+On its first run, the launcher (`bin/hk`) downloads the prebuilt `hk` binary for
+your platform from GitHub Releases and verifies its SHA256. It caches the binary
+under `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`. After that, each hook is a single `exec`.
+Prebuilt targets: Linux (musl) and macOS for x86_64 and aarch64, and Windows
+(MSVC) for x86_64 and aarch64.
+
+To build from source instead, or if the download is not possible:
+
+```
+cargo install --git https://github.com/Rixmerz/hook-n-hooks hk
+```
+
+The launcher uses an `hk` on `PATH` when its version matches the plugin's. You
+can also point it at a binary with `HK_BIN=/path/to/hk`.
+
+**Windows:** Claude Code runs hook commands through Git Bash, which the launcher
+needs. Without Git Bash, Claude Code has no Bash tool, so there are no Bash
+commands to compact. Formatting and the repo map then need `HK_BIN` set or an
+`hk.exe` on `PATH`. See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#windows).
+
+## Permissions
+
+Claude Code checks permission rules against the rewritten command, not the one
+Claude wrote. Before it rewrites a command, `hk` checks the original command
+against your own rules in `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` and
+`.claude/settings.local.json`:
+
+- **A `deny` or `ask` rule matches:** the command is not rewritten, so your rule
+  keeps working.
+- **An `allow` rule matches** (for example `Bash(cargo test:*)`): the command is
+  rewritten, and `hk` passes your decision on as `allow`. `hk` never allows a
+  command your rules did not allow.
+- **No rule matches:** in `auto` and `bypassPermissions` mode the command is
+  rewritten and Claude Code's normal checks still apply. In other modes it is
+  left alone, so the approval prompt shows the command Claude wrote. To change
+  this, set `rewrite.unapproved = "rewrite"`.
+
+Rules you pass on the command line (`--allowedTools`) and managed settings are
+not visible to hooks.
+
+## Configuration
+
+`hk` works without configuration. To change it, add an optional
+`.claude/hk.toml` to the project. Every key is optional:
+
+```toml
+[filters]          # turn individual filters off
+pytest = true
+install = false
+
+[limits]
+generic_max_lines = 80   # generic filter: truncate above this many lines
+head = 30
+tail = 30
+max_errors = 20          # diagnostics/failures listed before "+N more"
+stack_lines = 5          # context lines kept per failing test
+
+[rewrite]
+enabled = true
+generic_commands = ["make", "just"]   # also wrap these with the generic filter
+unapproved = "skip"                   # or "rewrite"; see Permissions
+
+[format]
+enabled = true
+
+[session_start]
+enabled = true
+```
+
+## Stats
+
+```
+$ hk stats
+Estimated tokens saved: 218 over 2 run(s) (1248 -> 376 chars, tokens = chars/4)
+
+filter             runs tokens saved
+cargo_test            1          145
+pytest                1           72
+```
+
+Each wrapped run appends one line to `stats.jsonl` in the data directory:
+`~/.local/share/hk` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/hk` on macOS, and
+`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hk` on Windows. The estimate is characters / 4. Raw output is
+capped at 30,000 characters, the length at which Claude Code truncates Bash
+output itself. The printed log line counts as output. Logs are pruned to the
+latest 200.
+
+## Other commands
+
+```
+hk run [--filter NAME] -- <cmd> [args...]   # use a filter by hand
+hk filters                                  # list filters
+hk map [DIR]                                # print the SessionStart repo map
+```
+
+## Documentation
+
+- [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): how it works, the verified hook
+  schema, and the design decisions
+- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): how to add a filter and its fixtures
+- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) and [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)
+
+## License
+
+Dual-licensed under [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or [Apache-2.0](LICENSE-APACHE), at your
+option.

@@ -0,0 +1,237 @@
+# Architecture
+
+`hook-n-hooks` is a Claude Code plugin made of two parts. One is a few JSON
+manifests. The other is a single Rust binary, `hk`, that every hook calls. The
+binary parses JSON in-process and never spawns `jq`, `grep` or a shell to make
+its decisions. A hook invocation takes about 1 ms plus process start-up.
+
+```
+.claude-plugin/plugin.json       plugin manifest
+.claude-plugin/marketplace.json  this repo is also its own marketplace
+hooks/hooks.json                 SessionStart, PreToolUse(Bash), PostToolUse(Edit|Write|MultiEdit)
+bin/hk                           POSIX sh launcher: find or download the binary, then exec it
+crates/hk/                       the binary
+  src/filters/                   one module per tool family, plus the registry
+  src/run.rs                     `hk run`: execute, tee the log, compact, keep the exit code
+  src/hook.rs                    hook handlers (all fail open)
+  src/permissions.rs             mirrors the user's Bash rules for the original command
+  src/shell.rs                   conservative parsing of simple Bash commands
+  src/format.rs                  per-file format and autofix
+  src/repomap.rs, src/stack.rs   SessionStart map, stack detection
+  src/stats.rs, src/paths.rs     local stats and data directory
+  tests/fixtures/<tool>/         real captured outputs
+  tests/snapshots/               insta snapshots of the compacted outputs
+```
+
+## What the docs say (verified)
+
+The design rests on the official documentation, read on 2026-11-23 at
+<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks> (docs.claude.com redirects there),
+<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference> and
+<https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces>.
+
+Not everything was read. The last ~14k characters of the hooks page were not,
+and neither was the separate marketplace-reference page (the full `owner` and
+`source` schemas). Anything below that relies on those parts is marked
+*unverified*.
+
+### PreToolUse
+
+- Output: `hookSpecificOutput` with `hookEventName: "PreToolUse"`,
+  `permissionDecision` (`allow|deny|ask|defer`), `permissionDecisionReason`,
+  `updatedInput` and `additionalContext`.
+- **`updatedInput` exists, and it replaces the whole input object.** For Bash we
+  therefore copy every field (`command`, `description`, `timeout`,
+  `run_in_background`) and change only `command`.
+- `permissionDecision` is not required alongside `updatedInput`.
+- **Permission rules are evaluated against the input the hook returns.** We
+  checked this end to end with `claude -p --plugin-dir`. With
+  `--allowedTools 'Bash(cargo test:*)'`, the rewritten command was refused with
+  "This command requires approval". The same run with a project
+  `allow: ["Bash(cargo test:*)"]` succeeded, because `hk` restated the allow.
+  Auto mode accepted the rewritten command. See [Permissions](#permissions).
+- Exit code 2 blocks the tool call. `hk` never exits 2.
+
+### PostToolUse
+
+- Top level: `decision: "block"` and `reason`.
+  `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is also available.
+- `updatedToolOutput` exists (and is preferred over `updatedMCPToolOutput`). It
+  can replace what Claude sees from a built-in tool, after the tool has run.
+- **A failed tool call fires `PostToolUseFailure`, which cannot rewrite
+  results.** A Bash command that exits non-zero is the case where compaction
+  saves the most, so rewriting output in PostToolUse would miss exactly that
+  case. That is why Bash compaction rewrites the command in PreToolUse
+  (`hk run -- <cmd>`) instead.
+- For Edit/Write we only add `additionalContext`.
+
+### SessionStart
+
+- Claude Code adds a SessionStart hook's plain-text stdout to Claude's context.
+  `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` also works. `hk` prints plain text.
+- Each field is capped at 10,000 characters. The map is capped at 4,000.
+
+### Input
+
+- Common fields: `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`,
+  `hook_event_name`. Tool events add `tool_name`, `tool_input` and
+  `tool_use_id`. PostToolUse adds `tool_response`.
+- Command hooks must print only the JSON object on stdout.
+
+### Plugins
+
+- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` requires only `name`. `hooks/hooks.json` needs
+  the top-level `"hooks"` wrapper.
+- `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the installed plugin directory, which changes on
+  update. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is `~/.claude/plugins/data/<id>/`, which
+  survives updates and is removed on uninstall. Both are also set as environment
+  variables for hook processes.
+- On Windows, shell-form hook commands run through Git Bash, or through
+  PowerShell when Git Bash is missing. Without Git Bash the Bash tool is not
+  registered.
+- Marketplace: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with `name`, `owner` and
+  `plugins[]` (`name`, `source`). A relative `source` is resolved from the
+  marketplace root. `claude plugin validate .` passes on this repository.
+
+## Bash compaction
+
+1. **PreToolUse** gets `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"cargo test"}}`.
+2. `shell::parse` accepts only *simple* commands: an optional `cd DIR &&`
+   prefix, optional `NAME=value` assignments, then plain words. Pipes,
+   redirections, `;`, `&&` chains, `$(...)`, backticks, subshells, background
+   `&` and newlines are all left alone. So are `run_in_background` and watch
+   modes (`--watch`, bare `vitest`, `dev`, `serve`).
+3. The filter registry picks the filter that owns the command.
+4. `permissions.rs` checks the original command against the user's rules (see
+   below).
+5. The command becomes
+   `cd DIR && NAME=v '<abs path to hk>' run --filter F --session S -- <original words>`.
+   The `cd` and the assignments stay in the parent shell, so the Bash tool's
+   working directory still carries over to later commands. The original words
+   are passed verbatim, so Bash still does the real quoting and expansion. `hk`
+   gets an argv and runs it directly, with no shell, so the same code runs on
+   every OS. On Windows, `.cmd` shims (npm, pnpm, npx) found on `PATH` run
+   through `cmd /C`.
+6. **`hk run`** prints `[hk] log: <path>` first and flushes it. Then it merges
+   the child's stdout and stderr into one pipe (`std::io::pipe`), which keeps
+   their interleaving. Every chunk is teed to the log as it arrives, so a
+   timeout kill still leaves the path in Claude's output and the log on disk.
+   Stdin is inherited.
+7. When the child exits, the cleaned output goes to the filter.
+   `text::clean` strips ANSI, normalises CRLF, and collapses `\r` progress
+   redraws. If the filter returns `None`, or a result that is not shorter than
+   the input, the generic filter is used. `hk` then prints the result, appends
+   a stats record, and exits with **the child's exact exit code**: on Unix,
+   `128 + signal` for a signal; on Windows, the full 32-bit code, through
+   `process::exit`.
+
+### Golden rule
+
+Any output Claude sees from a wrapped command starts with the path to the full
+raw log. Logs live in the data directory (`logs/`), and the latest 200 are kept.
+
+## Filter registry
+
+```rust
+pub trait Filter: Sync {
+    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
+    fn detect(&self, cmd: &Cmd) -> bool;
+    fn filter(&self, output: &str, exit: i32, limits: &Limits) -> Option<String>;
+}
+```
+
+`Cmd` is the effective program and its arguments. Wrappers such as `npx`,
+`bunx`, `pnpm exec`, `uv run`, `poetry run` and `python -m` are already removed,
+and paths and `.exe` are stripped from the program name. Filters are listed in
+`filters::registry()`, in priority order. To add a tool, see
+[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
+
+## Permissions
+
+The rewrite changes the command string that permission rules are matched
+against. Left as it is, that would cause two problems. It would cause extra
+approval prompts for commands the user already allowed. Worse, it would bypass
+`deny` and `ask` rules, such as `Bash(npm install:*)`. So before rewriting,
+`permissions.rs` reads the `permissions.{allow,deny,ask}` arrays from
+`~/.claude/settings.json`, `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/settings.json` and
+`.claude/settings.local.json`, and checks the **original** command:
+
+| Original matches | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| `deny` or `ask` (matched loosely) | no rewrite |
+| `allow` (matched strictly) | rewrite, and return `permissionDecision: "allow"` with the rule in the reason |
+| nothing, in `auto` or `bypassPermissions` mode | rewrite with no decision; Claude Code's checks still apply |
+| nothing, in another mode | no rewrite (`rewrite.unapproved = "rewrite"` changes this) |
+
+With a `cd`/env prefix, only a catch-all `Bash` rule is restated as allow.
+Rules from `--allowedTools` and managed settings are not visible to hooks, so
+they are not mirrored. A command allowed only through `--allowedTools` is
+therefore not rewritten in default mode.
+
+## PostToolUse formatting
+
+Only the touched file is passed to any tool, and a tool runs only if it is
+found: first in `node_modules/.bin` (walking up from the file), then on `PATH`.
+`which` is implemented in-process.
+
+| Extension | Tools |
+| --- | --- |
+| `.rs` | `rustfmt --emit stdout` fed through **stdin**, so it cannot follow `mod foo;` into other files. The edition comes from the nearest `Cargo.toml`; the file is written only if it changed |
+| `.go` | `gofmt -w` |
+| `.py`, `.pyi` | `ruff check --fix`, then `ruff format` |
+| js/ts/json/css/vue/svelte | `biome check --write` if present; otherwise `prettier --write` and `eslint --fix --format unix` |
+
+If the file changed, the context says so ("re-read before editing again"),
+because Claude's copy is now stale. Unfixed issues are listed, capped at
+`max_errors`. If there is nothing to report, the hook prints nothing.
+
+## SessionStart map
+
+`stack.rs` detects `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` (package manager from the
+lockfile; scripts `build`/`test`/`lint`; `tsconfig.json`), `deno.json[c]`
+(tasks), `pyproject.toml` (uv/poetry runner; ruff) and `go.mod`. `repomap.rs`
+prints the stacks, the resolved commands, and a 2-level tree, with directories
+first, at most 15 entries per directory, and vendored or build directories
+skipped.
+
+## Data, stats, privacy
+
+Logs and `stats.jsonl` live in a fixed per-OS directory (`paths.rs`), because
+`hk run` runs inside the Bash tool, which does not see `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA`, and
+`hk stats` runs from your terminal. `HK_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Tokens are
+estimated as `chars / 4`. Raw output is capped at 30,000 characters (Claude
+Code's default Bash output limit) before computing savings, so the stats do not
+overclaim. Nothing is sent anywhere.
+
+## Distribution
+
+`bin/hk` is a POSIX `sh` launcher:
+
+1. `$HK_BIN` if it is set;
+2. the cached `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/bin/<version>/hk[.exe]`;
+3. an `hk` on `PATH` whose `hk version` matches;
+4. a download of `hk-<target>[.exe]` and `.sha256` from the `v<version>` GitHub
+   Release (curl, wget or PowerShell), verified with sha256sum, shasum or
+   certutil, then an atomic move into the cache.
+
+If every step fails, `hk hook …` exits 0 with no output (fail open). The reason
+goes to stderr, along with the `cargo install` fallback.
+
+### Windows
+
+Claude Code runs shell-form hook commands through Git Bash on Windows, so the
+`sh` launcher works there. Without Git Bash, Claude Code has no Bash tool, so
+Bash compaction does not apply anyway. The PowerShell fallback cannot run an
+extension-less `sh` script. Users without Git Bash need `hk.exe` on `PATH`, from
+`cargo install`, and then the formatting and SessionStart hooks have to point to
+it. A PowerShell launcher is on the roadmap. Release assets use the MSVC targets
+for x86_64 and aarch64.
+
+## Known limits
+
+- Only simple commands are rewritten. `cargo test 2>&1 | tail` is passed
+  through untouched.
+- `hk run` buffers the output for the filter; the log is written as the output
+  arrives. Watch modes are never wrapped.
+- Filters are heuristic. Anything a filter does not recognise falls back to
+  generic head/tail, which is never worse than the raw output plus one log line.
